benchmark_progress: Unblocks the WL-B1 'pass the project build/test gates' criterion: legacy-HTML article rendering no longer crashes the server bundle (the isomorphic-dompurify -> jsdom -> html-encoding-sniffer -> @exodus/bytes ESM-require chain is fully removed from the dependency graph), and `pnpm test` is wired up and green (10/10) for the first time in this repository, including catching and fixing a dormant routes-validation bug that had never been able to run. Does not itself address the separate WL-B1 fail-closed-build/snapshot criteria, which remain scoped to WL-BUILD-001 (PR #29, open, unmerged).

tests.detail: __tests__/article-content.test.ts (new, 7 tests): jsdom-free import guard, Markdown passthrough, <script>/event-handler stripping on legacy HTML fixtures modeled on the two production-affected slugs, javascript: URL stripping, benign-formatting preservation, safe-fallback-not-raw-HTML on strip-to-empty, empty-content handling. __tests__/routes.test.ts (converted from unrunnable Jest-style globals to node:test; 3 tests) now passes after removing the dead/incorrect ROUTES.RESOURCES constant from lib/routes.ts.

builds.build: pnpm build (Next.js 16.2.6, Turbopack) -> succeeded, all 40 pages generated
builds.lint: pnpm lint -> fails repo-wide with a pre-existing, unrelated ESLint 9 flat-config migration error (ESLint couldn't find eslint.config.js); not touched, out of scope, already noted in open PR #29
builds.bundle_check: grep of .next/server compiled output confirms zero references to isomorphic-dompurify/jsdom/html-encoding-sniffer/@exodus/bytes; sanitize-html present instead

defects_found: Production crash (issue #24): isomorphic-dompurify's jsdom dependency chain requires @exodus/bytes (pure ESM) via CJS require() inside html-encoding-sniffer@6, which throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM on Node runtimes below the synchronous-require(esm) support line (Node < 20.19 / < 22.12) -- exactly the runtimes @exodus/bytes's own package.json 'engines' field excludes.

Adjacent security defect in the original prepareContent(): when the strict DOMPurify allowlist stripped an article to empty output, the code fell back to raw, unsanitized HTML -- silently defeating sanitization in exactly the highest-risk case (content the allowlist judged unsafe/malformed enough to remove entirely).

Dormant test-suite bug: __tests__/routes.test.ts used Jest-style describe/it/expect globals with no test runner ever configured in package.json, so it never actually ran. Once wired to node:test, it correctly failed on a real bug: lib/routes.ts exported ROUTES.RESOURCES = '/resources' as a 'valid' route, even though next.config.mjs permanently redirects /resources -> /city-resources.
defects_fixed: Removed isomorphic-dompurify entirely (package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml) and replaced it with sanitize-html in the new lib/article-content.ts, eliminating the jsdom/ESM dependency chain from the runtime and the compiled server bundle.

Closed the raw-HTML fallback hole: prepareArticleContent() now re-sanitizes with sanitize-html's permissive safe defaults when the strict allowlist yields empty output, and returns empty content (not raw DB content) on any sanitizer error.
Removed the unused/incorrect ROUTES.RESOURCES constant from lib/routes.ts so VALID_ROUTES no longer lists a redirect source as a valid route.
Converted __tests__/routes.test.ts to node:test/node:assert so it actually executes.
proposed_follow_up_missions: Once WL-BUILD-001 (PR #29) merges and a production content snapshot exists, run the full V5-plan legacy-HTML-to-Markdown ingestion migration described in issue #24, removing the HTML-rendering/dangerouslySetInnerHTML path from app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx entirely rather than only swapping its sanitizer.
Add an 'engines' field to package.json (e.g. >=20.19.0 or >=22.12.0) as defense-in-depth so any future ESM-only transitive dependency fails fast in CI instead of only in Vercel's production runtime.
Separately fix the repo-wide ESLint 9 flat-config migration (pnpm lint currently fails immediately with no config file found) -- unrelated to this mission, already noted in PR #29.

challenge_pass.real_objective: Eliminate the production ERR_REQUIRE_ESM crash on /blog/[slug] for legacy HTML articles (issue #24) without weakening XSS protection, and add regression tests that would have caught this class of bug before it reached production -- not merely make the named library (isomorphic-dompurify) go away.
hidden_assumptions: That the crash is inherent to running any jsdom-based sanitizer under Node generally. It is not: it is conditional on the Node runtime version. @exodus/bytes (pulled in transitively via html-encoding-sniffer -> jsdom -> dompurify) is pure ESM and declares engines '^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=24.0.0' because it relies on Node's synchronous require(esm) support; below that, any require() reaching it throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM exactly as seen in production.

That a local repro attempt would straightforwardly reproduce the crash. It did not: this sandbox's Node v22.22.2 is new enough to support require(esm), so `require('isomorphic-dompurify')` and even `require('jsdom')` succeeded cleanly here. Trusting that negative result would have wrongly suggested the bug was already fixed or unreproducible.

That the existing 'sanitized output is empty -> fall back to raw HTML' branch in the original code was an intentional, acceptable resilience choice. It is not: it silently serves attacker/DB-controlled raw HTML exactly when the allowlist judged the content least safe.

That adding regression tests requires adopting a test framework (vitest/jest) as a new dependency, as the parallel open PR #29 does. Node 22 ships a native `node --test` runner with unflagged TypeScript type-stripping, so zero-dependency tests are possible and avoid a second, competing test-framework introduction landing alongside PR #29's.
challenge_pass.obvious_path: Swap isomorphic-dompurify for sanitize-html in-place inside app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx, keeping the same ALLOWED_TAGS/ALLOWED_ATTR contract -- exactly the interim fix issue #24 itself names ('use a Node-native server sanitizer such as sanitize-html').
challenge_pass.optimized_path: Same library swap, plus: (a) extracted into standalone lib/article-content.ts so the sanitizer is unit-testable without booting the RSC/React tree or a live Supabase connection; (b) closed the raw-HTML fallback hole (re-sanitize with safe defaults instead of returning raw content); (c) fixed the dormant, never-executed routes test it surfaced once actually run; (d) added a zero-dependency `node --test` script rather than a new test framework.
challenge_pass.non_obvious_path: Do the full V5-plan fix instead of a sanitizer swap: normalize legacy HTML article rows to Markdown once, at content-ingestion time (a one-time batch job against Supabase), and delete the HTML-rendering/dangerouslySetInnerHTML path from app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx entirely, so no HTML sanitizer of any kind runs on every request ever again.
challenge_pass.cheapest_reversible_test: Before touching next.config.mjs or attempting a full production build, directly introspect the failing require chain locally (node_modules/.pnpm/{jsdom,html-encoding-sniffer,@exodus+bytes}/.../package.json engines/type fields and their require() call sites) and unit-test the new sanitizer module with `node --test` against fixtures modeled on the two production-affected slugs (script tags, onclick handlers, javascript: URLs) plus a Markdown fixture -- seconds, fully offline, fully reversible, and directly discriminates whether the fix both sanitizes correctly and removes the ESM-require risk, without needing a live Supabase connection or a Vercel deploy.
challenge_pass.alternate_access_surfaces: No external data source was needed for the fix itself; the original crash evidence came from Vercel production runtime logs already quoted verbatim in issue #24 (this sandbox has no Vercel API/log access). For root-causing *why* it crashed, local package-manager introspection (pnpm-resolved node_modules/.pnpm metadata) substituted for a live Vercel repro, since this sandbox's own Node version is new enough not to reproduce the failure directly.
challenge_pass.existing_assets_or_open_source: sanitize-html (mature, MIT-licensed, no DOM/jsdom dependency) was reused as-is -- it is the exact library issue #24 names as the preferred interim fix. react-markdown + remark-gfm (already a dependency, already used by ArticleRenderer for the Markdown path) were left untouched. Node's built-in node:test/node:assert runner was reused instead of adding vitest or jest.
challenge_pass.human_in_loop_option: The mission's own merge_policy (owner_required) is the human-in-the-loop gate already in force for this change; no additional manual workflow is cheaper or safer than an automated, fully-tested, offline-reversible library swap.
challenge_pass.recommendation: Ship the sanitize-html swap now (obvious/optimized path, this PR). Defer the HTML-to-Markdown ingestion migration (non-obvious path) until WL-BUILD-001's snapshot baseline is merged, per issue #24's own explicit sequencing rule ('Do not write conversion changes to production before the snapshot/rollback baseline exists').
assumptions_challenged: That the crash is Node-version-independent and would reproduce in any Node environment -- disproved by direct testing in this sandbox (Node 22.22.2 does not crash on the same require chain).
That the original 'fall back to raw HTML on empty/error' behavior was safe resilience rather than a sanitization bypass -- rejected and fixed.
That fixing the crash necessarily means adding a new test-framework dependency -- rejected in favor of Node's built-in test runner.
That the dormant routes.test.ts was passing/irrelevant -- disproved once actually executed; it caught a real bug (ROUTES.RESOURCES).

route_comparison.tradeoffs: Small, local, fully offline-testable diff; removes jsdom/ESM-require risk entirely and permanently regardless of future Node/Vercel runtime choices; preserves the existing HTML-content code path and visual output for legacy articles; does not reduce the request-time sanitization cost or remove dangerouslySetInnerHTML as an architectural surface.

route_comparison.route: B: pin Node/Vercel runtime via package.json 'engines' to >=20.19.0/>=22.12.0, leave isomorphic-dompurify in place
route_comparison.tradeoffs: Possibly a one-line fix if Vercel actually reads and applies the engines field for this project (it can), but unverifiable from this sandbox (no Vercel dashboard/API access, no evidence of the project's currently configured runtime); does not fix the separately-found raw-HTML-fallback security defect; leaves the repo dependent on a specific upstream package's ESM/CJS choices never regressing again. Rejected as the primary fix; recommended as a defense-in-depth follow-up regardless of route A.

route_comparison.route: C: full legacy-HTML-to-Markdown ingestion migration (non-obvious path)
route_comparison.tradeoffs: Permanently removes the entire HTML-sanitizer-on-every-request architecture and its attack surface, not just one library's crash; but requires a live Supabase connection this sandbox does not have, requires the not-yet-merged snapshot/rollback baseline (WL-BUILD-001/PR #29) that issue #24 itself lists as a hard precondition, and is a data-model migration, not this mission's stated objective. Deferred, not rejected outright -- proposed as a follow-up mission.

challenge_pass.material_difference: Route C differs from Route A/B in mechanism, not just wording: it changes the canonical storage format of article content (HTML rows become Markdown), moves sanitization cost from 'every request, forever' to 'one batch job, once', and removes the dangerouslySetInnerHTML/HTML-sanitizer surface from the runtime entirely for migrated content, rather than narrowing which library sits behind that same surface.
challenge_pass.validation_result: pnpm test (node --test): 10/10 passing, covering XSS-payload stripping on legacy-HTML fixtures modeled on the two production-affected slugs, javascript:-URL stripping, the strip-to-empty safe-fallback path, Markdown passthrough, and empty-content handling. npx tsc --noEmit: clean. pnpm build (Next.js 16.2.6, Turbopack): succeeded, all 40 routes generated. Static analysis of the compiled .next/server bundle confirms zero remaining references to isomorphic-dompurify/jsdom/html-encoding-sniffer/@exodus/bytes, with sanitize-html present instead. Separately confirmed in this sandbox's Node 22.22.2 that `require('jsdom')` and `require('isomorphic-dompurify')` do NOT crash here, evidencing that the bug is Node-runtime-version-conditional and that a naive local repro would have been misleading.
